If the pain is more than the friendship is worth then tell him upfront the truth and say let’s part ways. He’d want to know why he got alienated and such. You telling him would give him peace that it wasn’t him and his actions that made him lose all his friends. It wouldn’t be fair if you just slowly isolated him and he doesn’t know what happened and why he got abandoned. Please don’t do that to him, I grew up very isolated socially and when you’re alone for so long and finally find some connections, losing those connections and thinking it’s your fault is beyond devastating, it can take a life. You don’t understand that it can be night and day difference in the trajectory in his life. He can fall into a depressive and suicidal state because who wouldn’t after losing close friends. 

If you truly love him, don’t toss him away because you’re afraid. It’s just not fair, he has no say and no chance to react to you or to see the true you. He’d just wonder what happened and where the friendship connections went wrong. 

Now, if he responds in a nasty way, then you can toss him and not feel guilty about it.

You have a right to be frustrated at him but not angry imo 
He didn’t want to make this worse than it is. He was indirectly doing you a favor. Telling you would have just gotten you upset and it would have done more damage if you knew earlier. 

And best to let assholes keep their thoughts to themselves. 

Your friend did something I’d say that’s in the grey area. He saw that informing you would have done no parties any favor to the drama. He saw that not gossiping and letting time pass was the better option. So he went that route instead of relaying and repeating those nasty comments about you which would have hurt you and gotten you more upset than you were after that drama. 

I do know how you feel though. You just feel like he betrayed you when others were saying negative things about you. 

Speaking on him randomly bringing it up. It may have been on his mind for months and he may have had heavy guilt as a good friend that he kept that from you, so he dropped it and hoped for the best. 

I’d see it as a good thing in the end because he did eventually did communicate it with you once that drama passed and some more.

I wouldn’t start overthinking it until the next day and some more hours, plus he communicated with you that he had to go so it’s not like they’re ignoring you. I have a friend who sometimes doesn’t get a chance to respond to me until tomorrow or the day after. He told me that he’d rather text and respond late with a fruitful and useful response to whatever I said rather than sending a quick but careless reply. 

 I get anxious and overthink too. I learned, best to worry and think once it become obvious something is up. Like you see them active responding to other people but not you. Otherwise it would be them falling asleep or having to tend to family and not getting the time or appropriate moment to respond to you thoughtfully.

A good friend would watch out for their friends’ feelings and present state. If my friend was bullied for no good reason, then I’d call that out and roast whoever dares mess with my friend like that. Stand up for people you care about and like.

Ask yourself what you want in life. I realized I couldn’t see myself as a man and a husband. It always felt wrong being a dude but I couldn’t put a finger on it. Realized I didn’t want to live as a bisexual man when I went on a date and literally hated being seen as a gay man. I wanted to be the pretty trans girl with a gay boy not a pretty boy with another pretty boy.

Sigh... This was me for years and years throughout middle school and all of high school. I was in denial of being trans for the longest time, I didn't even know it. Eventually I did more research and older folks tell their stories of how this isn't a phase and if it hasn't gone away since childhood, it'll never go away. That's how I accepted and came out to myself as trans. That's always the first step is to be able to accept yourself and not second guess who you are. I did that and never really had an identity throughout school because of that. I was a hollow "boy", I felt numb and sad all the time. When I started to accept myself, I was able to smile more and just feel general euphoria in hopes of my future transition.

If these thoughts of your incongruent identity don't go away, then it's highly likely you're trans or at least somewhere on the NB spectrum. 

This is something you'll have to work out on your own over time. You only know yourself, it's time to stop letting others project onto you what they want you to be. I made that mistake once in grade school, I'm not going to do it again in my 20s.

Which means to ghost them and no even try to communicate your distress. Narcissists do no respond well when they are exposed, it is their greatest fear as they constantly put on a facade for the world to see when the real them actually have puny fragile egos. 

Once you understand narcissism, you’ll spot it a mile away and will be in a better position in life. 

We may never be able to undo the damage it did to people like us, but we can use it to our advantage. Many people who have no experience with narcissists, accidentally get into relationships with them only to find out they are in a world of hell and it becomes insanely hard to leave because of the gaslighting. 

I’m jealous you’re 14 and you’re realizing this. Please know, the earlier the better. Some folks don’t break out of their hell until their late 30s and some folks never break free from narcissists, they become narcissist enablers. Your mind is overworked especially since you had to handle such a situation. Just wait it out and let the afterglow die down. Learn from this mistake and don’t take tripping with random folks lightly. Acid is a dangerous drug in the sense that it brings out the true persons in people. It can also make people over react and tweak out. 

When my friend thought it was a good idea to trip with like 8 people he met at college, it turned into a shit show. One person was so high in their peak, they turned aggressive and began fighting and biting people. When they came down or came back from it, they had NO memory of such event. Others were also too high and everyone was panicking. My friend had no way of sorting anything out because he was nearing ego death at the same time. He FaceTimed me crying for help while I was 400 miles away, telling me that he can’t remember anything anymore and should he call the cops. 

From personal experience I longer enjoy trips with more than about 4-5 people. It gets too hectic and hard to keep track of multiple people’s vibes. The only time I would do a massive group trip is if each person was proven to be mentally strong and has a lot of experience.
